title: The Morning Dawns upon the Place
description: The Morning Dawns upon the Place in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 227 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ's Passion”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The morn-ing dawns up-on the place, Where Je-sus spent the night in prayer; Through bright-ening glooms be-hold his face, No form or come-li-ness is there.

lines: The morning dawns upon the place,
Where Jesus spent the night in prayer;
Through brightening glooms behold his face,
No form or comeliness is there.
Last eve by those he called his own,
In all their malice, rage, and pride.
But hark! he prays; — 'tis for his foes;
He speaks; — 'tis comfort to his friends;
"Truly, this was the Son of God!"
— Though in a servant's mean disguise,
And bruised beneath the Father's rod,
Not for himself, — for man he dies.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
